# homarr_board_copy (Resource)

Creates a Homarr board by copying an existing one, tiles included, and then manages the copy like `homarr_board`.

Homarr's REST API cannot read tiles back, so `homarr_board` can only create empty boards. Copying (`POST /api/boards/{id}/duplicate`, present since Homarr 2.0.0) is the way to reproduce a board designed in the UI: design a template there once, then stamp out copies with Terraform. Everything on the source is copied in one transaction — its appearance settings and visibility, every layout with its column and gutter counts, the sections, and the tiles with their options, positions and integration links. The copy belongs to the user behind the API key.

~> **The copy is a snapshot, not a sync.** Later changes to the source are not carried over, and the copied content — tiles, layouts, column counts, appearance — is neither refreshed nor compared afterwards. Only `name`, `is_public`, `is_home` and `is_mobile_home` are managed; use `homarr_board_settings` to override the inherited appearance.

~> **Replacing a copy discards everything done to it since.** A new `source_board_id` destroys the copy, with any tiles added or moved in the UI, and copies the source afresh under a new id, which also changes everything that references it, such as `homarr_server_board_settings`. That includes the source being replaced: if the template is a `homarr_board` whose `column_count` changes, every copy of it is replaced too. Add `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [source_board_id] }` to keep copies through that.

Homarr checks the whole source while copying, and refuses the copy when:

* the API key lacks the `board-create` permission, or view access to the source — the latter answered with 404, like a missing board;
* a tile links an integration the key's user may not *use* (404 `Integration not found`);
* a tile is a widget that requires an integration but has none — as happens when its only integration is deleted, which unlinks it silently (400 `<kind> requires an integration`);
* the source contains custom widgets and the key is not an admin's.

Unlike `homarr_board`, a copy is never made its creator's home board automatically. App tiles on the copy point at the same `homarr_app` ids as the source's.

Renaming, changing `is_public` and destroying the copy need full access to it, which its creator always has.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Design a template board in the Homarr UI once, then stamp out copies of it,
# tiles included. The template can be any board the API key can view.
data "homarr_board" "template" {
  name = "team-template"
}

resource "homarr_board_copy" "team_a" {
  source_board_id = data.homarr_board.template.id
  name            = "team-a"

  # Inherited from the template when left out. A copy of a public template set
  # to false is public for a moment, until the visibility change lands.
  is_public = false
}

# A copy is a snapshot: later edits to the template are not carried over. Copies
# of a template managed in this configuration would be replaced whenever the
# template is (a column_count change, say), losing everything changed on them in
# the UI since. ignore_changes keeps them.
resource "homarr_board" "template" {
  name         = "ops-template"
  column_count = 12
}

resource "homarr_board_copy" "ops" {
  for_each = toset(["ops-eu", "ops-us"])

  source_board_id = homarr_board.template.id
  name            = each.key

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [source_board_id]
  }
}

# The inherited appearance can be overridden like any other board's.
resource "homarr_board_settings" "team_a" {
  board_id   = homarr_board_copy.team_a.id
  page_title = "Team A"
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the copy, also used in its URL. Same rules as `homarr_board`'s `name`: only ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_`, unique compared case-insensitively. Renaming happens in place. Homarr refuses a taken name when copying and renaming; the provider warns about one while planning.
- `source_board_id` (String) Identifier of the board to copy. The API key needs view access to it.

Homarr keeps no link from a copy to its source, so this cannot be read back. Changing it replaces the copy. After an import it is unknown to the provider, and the next apply records the configured value in place, without replacing the board.

### Optional

- `is_home` (Boolean) Whether the copy is the desktop home board of the user behind the API key. Behaves exactly like `is_home` on `homarr_board`, and shares its lock, so the two resources can hand the flag over within one apply. Setting it to `false` requires Homarr 2.3.0 or newer.
- `is_mobile_home` (Boolean) Whether the copy is the mobile home board of the user behind the API key. Behaves exactly like `is_mobile_home` on `homarr_board`.
- `is_public` (Boolean) Whether the copy is visible without authentication. Leave it out to keep whatever the copy inherited from the source and to ignore later changes made in the UI.

Homarr copies the source's visibility and offers no way to choose another one in the same call, so a copy of a public board set to `false` is public for the moment between the copy and the visibility change. Should that change fail, the copy stays public, with a warning saying so, until the next apply replaces it.

### Read-Only

- `creator_id` (String) Identifier of the user that created the copy: the user behind the API key, unless the copy was imported.
- `id` (String) Homarr-generated identifier of the copy.
- `logo_image_url` (String) Board logo URL, as reported by Homarr — inherited from the source unless `homarr_board_settings` sets another.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
# The identity is the plain board id; name=<name> works only as an import id.
# source_board_id is taken from your configuration by the first apply.
import {
  to = homarr_board_copy.team_a
  identity = {
    id = "vbx4ghr2d8owm0c1t5k3zqje"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) Homarr-generated identifier of the copy.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = homarr_board_copy.team_a
  id = "vbx4ghr2d8owm0c1t5k3zqje"
}

# Or by name, matched exactly first and then case-insensitively.
import {
  to = homarr_board_copy.ops["ops-eu"]
  id = "name=ops-eu"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A copy is imported by its board id, or by name as "name=<name>". Homarr keeps
# no record of which board a copy came from, so source_board_id is taken from
# your configuration by the first apply after the import, in place.
terraform import homarr_board_copy.team_a vbx4ghr2d8owm0c1t5k3zqje
terraform import homarr_board_copy.team_a name=team-a
```
